The '''card credits''' are the small printed lines on [[Players Committee]] [[Virtual cards]] that recognize the people and groups who contributed to a card: the person or group whose image the card uses ("Image courtesy of …"), the person or group who first proposed the card ("Original concept by …", often with the tournament or award where the concept was won), and the people a card is dedicated to ("In memory of …"). [[Decipher]]'s cards print no such credits; their pictures are film stills.

The list below gives everyone credited, alphabetically, with each card that credits them, the card's set and the credit as it is printed. It is generated from the card label data, so every credit in that data appears here.<ref name="labels">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/src/gemp-swccg-cards/src/main/resources/card_labels.json card_labels.json] in billbisco/swccg-gemp (commit 0bc4377d9): the printed labels of every Players Committee Virtual card, transcribed from the PC's card images. Field definitions: [https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/0bc4377d9dd48a100625e0ec75de6032d2ea92a1/docs/card_labels.md docs/card_labels.md].</ref><ref name="pcimages">Players Committee card images at res.starwarsccg.org (Virtual Sets 0–27, Virtual Premium and alternate images at 745 × 1039; Virtual Blocks 1–9 and Virtual Shields at 350 × 490), the source the card label data was read from. Each card's article shows its image.</ref>

== How to read this list ==
* Names are written exactly as printed. Where a credit names several people or groups, each has their own entry, and the card's row shows the whole printed line.
* A site or handle suffix ("@ ArtStation", "on DeviantArt", a web address) says where the work can be found; it is left out of the heading but kept in the printed line. A leading "the" is left out of the heading too.
* Differently printed names are not merged. When two headings may be the same person or group, each says "See also".
* Credit types: '''Concept''' ("Original concept by …"), '''Image''' ("Image courtesy of …" and similar), '''Featured in image''' (a person shown in a credited photo), '''In memory''' ("In memory of …").
